plan: Given my value of $21, the optimal bid is slightly below my value to maximize profit while still being competitive. Since the value is capped at $20, bidding slightly above $20 ensures winning, provided others bid based on their values. To avoid overpaying, I'll bid $20.1, aiming to win against a max $20 bid. This minimizes loss if others bid lower.

To maximize profit, I'll bid slightly above the average expected bid of competitors. My value is $16, so I'll aim to bid around $14. This ensures a profit margin if I win, given the worst-case scenario where the second-highest bid is just below mine. Bidding too high reduces my profit, while bidding too low risks losing the auction. With no history, I'll assume competitors bid near their values.

Given my private value of $17, I aim to maximize profit by winning the bid without overpaying. Since values are uniformly distributed between $0 and $20, I assume Andy and Betty might value the item similarly. To ensure a win, I should bid slightly above the average expected value, around $10. However, to avoid overpayment, I will bid slightly less than my value, at $15. This minimizes risk while maximizing potential profit, as I pay at most $15 but value at $17, ensuring a profit margin.
